t: A very cheap RISC-V chip with USB and USB-C power delivery built in.
steps: Buy a Polos CH32X035 breakout from AnalogLamb or a WeAct core board.
Install the Arduino IDE and add the WCH CH32 board package.
Plug in the board over USB-C and hold the boot button to enter the bootloader.
Upload the Blink example and watch an LED flash.
Try a USB device example from the ch32fun project on GitHub.
Try the USB PD sink example with a USB-C charger.
Study wagiminator's USB PD tester for a full project.
